::: {.why}
The tail index decides whether the variance exists at all, which decides whether half the machinery of the next four weeks applies to your data.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement the Hill estimator and state what it is estimating, including which moments exist for a given estimate.
- Show how much the estimate moves with the number of order statistics used, and say how you would report it honestly.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Implement the Hill estimator yourself in ten lines: sort the exceedances, take the mean log ratio to the threshold, invert. Apply it to the left and right tail of SPY separately.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Make the Hill plot: estimate against the number of upper order statistics k, for k from 20 to 500. Then say what you would report to someone who asked for one number, and why a single number without the plot is close to meaningless.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Draw the consequence: at your estimated index, say which moments exist. If the estimate is near or below 4, the sample kurtosis you computed yesterday is estimating something that does not exist, and that is the explanation for its instability.
:::
:::
